academic_translation:
Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom,
Even when the Victors have passed into nirvāṇa, their relics receive worship.
Therefore, whoever wishes to hold the qualities of the Victors
Should take up this perfection of wisdom; this is liberation.
translation: Supreme perfect wisdom has great good qualities. Because of this perfection, the relics of the Victorious Ones are honored even after they pass into the peace beyond sorrow. Anyone who wants to hold the good qualities of the Victorious Ones should take up this perfect wisdom. This is freedom.

Wisdom comes before giving generosity. It also comes before good conduct, patience, steady effort, and deep focus. Wisdom holds them all together so that these qualities of goodness are not wasted. This shows that all things share a single way.

academic_translation:
For example, in Jambudvīpa there are billions of trees,
Of various kinds, numerous types, and many forms;
Except for being spoken of as a number of shadows,
There are no diverse shadows, nor are there differences.
translation: For example, there are billions of trees in Jambudvipa. They have many different forms and kinds. We might talk about counting their many shadows. But the shadows themselves are not really different from one another.

academic_translation:
Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also
Attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom.
When dedicated for the sake of omniscience,
All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
translation: In the same way, the five perfections of the Victorious Ones get the very name of perfect wisdom. You can dedicate them for the sake of knowing everything. When you do, all six perfections share one taste. This one taste is called awakening.

academic_translation:
If a bodhisattva, while lacking full understanding,
Fully demonstrates form, perception, feeling, volition, and consciousness
As impermanent, they act upon a fabrication;
The wise never destroy phenomena.
translation: An awakening hero might not fully understand. They might teach that form, idea, feeling, intention, and awareness are always changing. But if they do, they act on a made-up idea. Wise people never destroy things.

academic_translation:
Where one does not take anything as form or feeling, and perception is not apprehended,
Nor is consciousness taken as such, and volition is not apprehended,
And all phenomena are fully known as unborn and empty—
This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: In this practice, you do not take anything as form or feeling. You do not find any idea. You do not take anything as awareness. You do not find any intention. You fully know that all things are never born and are empty. This is the practice of supreme perfect wisdom. It is the highest perfection.

academic_translation:
Compared to someone who, in fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
Tames all the sentient beings residing there to the state of an arhat,
Whoever writes down this perfection of wisdom
And gives the text to a supreme sentient being has far more exalted merit.
translation: Imagine someone travels to lands as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges. They help all the living beings there become a worthy one. But suppose someone else writes down this perfect wisdom and gives the book to a great person. That second person earns much more stored-up goodness. Sharing this perfection of wisdom is much better.

academic_translation:
Why is that? Those supreme speakers, having trained in this,
Demonstrate here that all phenomena are emptiness.
Hearing this, śrāvakas swiftly reach liberation,
And one reaches the awakening of a pratyekabuddha and the awakening of a Buddha.
translation: Why is that? The best speakers train in this. They show that all things are emptiness. When a listener hears this, they quickly reach freedom. This is how someone reaches the awakening of a solitary Buddha and a Buddha's awakening.

academic_translation:
If, without a sprout, a tree never emerges in the world,
How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it?
If, without the mind of awakening, a Victor does not emerge in the world,
How could the fruits—Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas—emerge?
translation: If a tree has no sprout, it will never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? It is the same without the wish to awaken. Without it, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. And without their awakening, how could the good fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?

academic_translation:
When the sun's disk radiates its web of light,
At that time sentient beings exert themselves in their work; likewise,
When the wise give rise in the world to the mind of awakening in order to know,
Through primordial wisdom, sentient beings become endowed with qualities.
translation: When the sun shines its light, living beings go to work. It is the same when wise people bring the wish to awaken into the world. They do this to know true awakening. Because of their deep knowing, living beings gain every good quality and wonderful quality.

academic_translation:
For example, if the lord of nāgas were not at Lake Anavatapta,
How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa?
If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge,
And in the ocean, too, there would not be many forms of jewels.
translation: Think about Lake Anavatapta. If the lord of the serpent spirits did not live there, how could rivers flow here in Jambudvipa? If there were no rivers, no flowers or fruits could grow. Without rivers, the ocean would not have many forms of jewels.

academic_translation:
Likewise, here too, without the mind of awakening, how could
The primordial wisdom of the Sugata emerge in all these worlds?
Without primordial wisdom, there is no increase of qualities and no awakening,
And the ocean-like qualities of a Buddha would also not exist.
translation: It is the same here. Without the wish to awaken, how could the deep knowing of the Well-Gone One appear in all these worlds? Without deep knowing, good qualities do not grow, and there is no awakening. Then a Buddha's qualities, which are like a great ocean, would not exist.

academic_translation:
However many illuminating creatures there are in this world,
Compared to the light emitted by all of them in order to illuminate,
A single ray of light emitted by the sun's disk is far superior;
All the lights of the host of illuminating ones cannot match a fraction of it.
translation: Think of all the glowing creatures in this world. Imagine all the light they shine together. A single ray of light from the sun is far better. All the light from those creatures cannot match even a tiny part of the sun's light.

academic_translation:
However much the hosts of śrāvakas, through generosity, ethical discipline,
And meditation, generate a fully endowed mass of merit,
Compared to a bodhisattva's single mind of rejoicing,
The heap of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match a fraction.
translation: All the listeners might gather a huge pile of stored-up goodness. They build this through generosity, good conduct, and meditation. But an awakening hero only needs a single thought to rejoice. The stored-up goodness of all those listeners cannot match a tiny part of the awakening hero's rejoicing.

academic_translation:
Whatever tens of millions of hundreds of billions of Buddhas of the past,
And those who abide in infinitely many thousands of tens of millions of fields,
And whatever Protectors of the World have passed into nirvāṇa,
Who teach the jewel Dharma in order to exhaust suffering—
translation: Think of the billions of Buddhas from the past. Think of those living right now in endless millions of lands. Think of all the Protectors of the world who have passed into the peace beyond sorrow. They all share the jewel teaching to end suffering.

academic_translation:
From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening,
Until the time the true Dharma of those Guides is exhausted,
Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval,
And whatever is endowed with the perfections, and whatever qualities of a Buddha—

locked_terms.use: make the wish for highest awakening

translation: Think of the time from when they first make the wish for highest awakening until the true teaching of those Guides comes to an end. Think of all the stored-up goodness those Victorious Ones have during that time. Think of everything that is filled with the perfections and a Buddha's qualities.

academic_translation:
And whatever is of the sons of the Buddhas and the śrāvakas,
The contaminated and uncontaminated virtues of ones in training and ones beyond training,
Having gathered them, the bodhisattva rejoices,
And dedicates them all for awakening as a cause for the benefit of beings.
translation: Think also of the goodness of the children of the Buddha and the listeners. This includes the stained goodness and the goodness free of impurity from both learners and ones who have finished learning. An awakening hero gathers all this goodness together and rejoices. Then they dedicate it all to awakening to help all beings.

academic_translation:
If, when dedicating, the perception of a mind arises,
And if there is the perception of awakening and the perception of sentient beings,
Because of these perceptions, dwelling in views, the mind is attached to the three;
Since there is apprehension, it does not amount to being dedicated.
translation: When they dedicate, the idea of a mind might arise. There might also be the idea of awakening and the idea of living beings. Because of these ideas, the mind stays in views and becomes attached to these three things. Because they treat them as something to hold onto, they do not truly dedicate.

academic_translation:
If one knows in this way that these phenomena cease and are exhausted,
And that to which one dedicates is also exhausted,
And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon,
By knowing perfectly in that way, it is dedicated.
translation: You might know that these things stop and fade away. The goal you dedicate them to fades away too. One of these things never dedicates to another of these things. If you understand this perfectly, then you truly dedicate.

academic_translation:
If one makes a sign of it, that is not dedicating;
But if there are no signs, it is the dedication to awakening.
Just like eating excellent food that is mixed with poison,
The Victor has taught that the apprehension of virtuous qualities is also like that.
translation: If you make a sign of it, you do not really dedicate it. But if there are no signs, it is the dedication to awakening. Think of eating excellent food that is mixed with poison. The Victorious One taught that seeing good things or any quality as something to hold onto is just like that.

academic_translation:
Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way:
Just as those Victors know that virtue—
Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its characteristic—
Rejoicing in it, one dedicates it in exactly that way.
translation: So, you should practice how to dedicate like this. The Victorious Ones fully know goodness. They know every way it appears, where it comes from, and its defining feature. You must rejoice in that goodness. Then you dedicate it in exactly the same way.

academic_translation:
If one dedicates merit to awakening in that way,
It is without poison, one does not abandon the Buddha, and one speaks what the Victor has spoken.
The hero dedicating in that way outshines
All the however many bodhisattvas in the world who are ones with apprehension.
translation: If you dedicate stored-up goodness to awakening like this, it has no poison. You stay close to the Buddha. You speak exactly what the Victorious One has said. A hero who dedicates in this way shines very bright. They outshine every awakening hero in the world who is one who holds onto something.

academic_translation:
Tens of millions of hundreds of billions of blind people without a guide,
Not even knowing the path, how could they enter the city?
Without wisdom, these five perfections are eyeless;
Being without a guide, they are unable to reach awakening.
translation: Imagine millions of blind people with no guide. They do not even know the path. How could they ever find the city? Without wisdom, these five perfections have no eyes. Because they have no guide, they cannot reach awakening.

academic_translation:
When they are perfectly embraced by wisdom,
They then gain eyes and obtain this name.
For example, just as a completed painting that lacks eyes
Earns no payment as long as the eyes are not painted.
translation: But when these practices are perfectly guided by wisdom, they gain eyes. Then they finally earn the name of perfections. Think of a beautiful painting that is missing its eyes. The artist earns no payment until the eyes are painted on.

academic_translation:
When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black phenomena
Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended,
In the world it is counted as the perfection of wisdom;
It is like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
translation: Wisdom breaks down things made by causes, things not made by causes, and good and bad things. You do not find even a tiny speck left. In the world, this perfection is known as perfect wisdom. It is like space, which does not rest on anything at all.

academic_translation:
If one thinks, "I shall practice the wisdom of the Victors,
And liberate many billions of sentient beings touched by suffering,"
Such a bodhisattva seeking awakening conceptually constructs the perception of sentient beings;
This is not practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.
translation: Someone might think, "I will practice the wisdom of the Victorious One. I will free billions of living beings touched by suffering." An awakening hero seeking awakening who holds onto the idea of living beings is not practicing the highest perfection, perfect wisdom.

academic_translation:
Any bodhisattva who, when practicing in the past,
Skillfully practiced this perfection and was without doubt,
Will, upon hearing it, immediately give rise to the perception of the Teacher;
They will swiftly realize peaceful awakening.
translation: Any awakening hero who practiced this perfection well in the past and had no doubts will right away form the idea of the Teacher when they hear about it now. They will quickly reach peaceful awakening.

academic_translation:
Even if one honored many billions of Buddhas when practicing in the past,
If one does not have faith in the Victors' perfection of wisdom,
Upon hearing it, that person of small intelligence will abandon it;
Having abandoned it, they will become without refuge and go to the Avīci hell.
translation: A person may have honored billions of Buddhas in the past. But they might not trust the perfect wisdom of the Victorious One. When a person with little understanding hears about this perfection, they will give it up. By giving it up, they will be left with no shelter and will go to the hell without rest.
